commits.edited_message:
Bound v4 sparse data buffer to the read element size in Mat_VarRead4

As reported by https://github.com/tbeu/matio/pull/313

The column dimension is validated against the index range of the
format when it is read back, so the duplicate guard before deriving
njc can never fire; drop it.

coupling: The defect lives in the v4 sparse reader (Mat_VarRead4, src/mat4.c) and is split across the two mat4.c maintenance commits. Commit 1 (0f282bf) removes the pre-existing column-dimension guard 'dims[1] > UINT_MAX - 1' that sits in front of 'sparse->njc = (mat_uint32_t)dims[1] + 1'; at that point in history the read-time validation above still caps dims at UINT_MAX-1, so the guard is genuinely dead code and its removal is correct. Commit 2 (e93ce24) rewrites the row/column dimension checks to be NaN-safe but, in doing so, widens the accepted upper bound from UINT_MAX-1 to UINT_MAX. Each edit is benign on its own (verified by execution): with only commit 1 the UINT_MAX-1 bound still prevents the overflow; with only commit 2 the old column guard still rejects dims[1]==UINT_MAX. Only together can a crafted v4 sparse file declare a column count of 4294967295 (UINT_MAX): it passes the widened check, the removed guard no longer fires, and njc = (uint32_t)UINT_MAX + 1 wraps to 0, so jc is allocated with size 0 and 'sparse->jc[0] = 0' writes 4 bytes into the zero-sized allocation (ASan heap-buffer-overflow WRITE). Neither single diff is wrong given the other side's original state - the safety invariant spans both commits - so a reviewer reading either commit alone sees correct-looking maintenance; recognizing the bug requires composing the guard removal in the first commit with the bound widening in the second.
